research_concepts: opponent next-possession PPP (downstream suppression) after play type X
regression to the mean and outcome-derived labels
methodological_questions: Is the opponent next-possession PPP shift after play X large enough to change AVOID labels, once direct PPP, game state and team quality are held fixed?
Do own-sequence lags (the same team's next 1-5 possessions) carry any within-team signal after team-season demeaning?
Are the play-type labels accurate enough for a downstream effect to be attributed to a play type?
Does the downstream effect mechanically depend on how play X ended (make, miss, turnover, foul), which fixes how the next possession starts?

historical_evidence.finding: Global lag curves for the same team's next 1-5 possessions showed flat, non-decaying lifts (e.g. SPOT_UP lag-1 +0.027, n=175,021). After team-season demeaning, within-team memory was essentially none except SPOT_UP lag-1. PNR lag-1 within-team lift was -0.0218. Recorded mechanism: C_artifact.

The Level 1 gate failed the decay sanity check. DRIVE lifts were flat (+0.015 to +0.021) and fell to +0.015 to -0.002 within team, with Cohen d about 0.01-0.03 and p~0 from n>150k. Callable play-type horizons = 0. Recorded verdict: failed_gate. Team-quality confounding is the recorded cause.

Opponent T+1 suppression was real for 4 of 8 play types: CUT +0.0220, TRANSITION +0.0145, SPOT_UP +0.0124, POST_UP +0.0194. DRIVE was not real (opponent ATT +0.0024). The record says downstream effects are small (~0.01-0.02 PPP) relative to direct PPP gaps, and that player-level downstream results are mostly non-findings after BH correction.

Across 52 series (104 playoff team-offense units), no durable pivot branches were found (durable_branches=[]). Median net swing (own PPP minus opponent next PPP) was CUT +0.36, TRANSITION +0.26, PULL_UP +0.09, PNR +0.04, SPOT_UP +0.02, POST_UP -0.22, DRIVE -0.27. The record calls the DRIVE and POST_UP negative net swing the durable aftershock finding. Recorded mechanism: B_powered_null for the pivot branches.

After the opponent runs play type X, a defensive aftershock was recorded for 8 of 8 play types, replicating in all games and playoffs (e.g. CUT +0.119, n=21,398; TRANSITION +0.135, n=26,262). The record lists small sample as a limitation. This is a different direction and estimand from the question as posed.

The label audit failed overall: OTHER 20.2% against a target under 10%, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, most play-type PPP above the benchmark band, and MIA identity checks failed. Foul possessions leak into OTHER. The record says the labels have systematic issues that undermine adaptation findings.
A suppression label selected on the outcome was mostly an RTM artifact. Apparent LLM skill was leakage, and what survives is small and noisy.
Star-level sequential suppression after a specific opponent play type (PUTBACK for 6+ stars) used cells with n_after of 32-95 and no multiplicity correction. Recorded mechanism: E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Global (pooled) matched-baseline lag curves as evidence of own-team action memory
failed_approaches.why: The flat non-decaying lifts disappeared after team-season demeaning (C_artifact). Only SPOT_UP lag-1 remained within team.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Level 1 decay-sanity gate for cross-possession memory
failed_approaches.why: Lifts were flat rather than decaying, and the effect collapsed under a within-team baseline. The record names a team-quality confound. Huge n made p-values uninformative (d about 0.01-0.03).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using outcome-selected suppression as a predictive label, and the apparent LLM edge
failed_approaches.why: The label was selected on the outcome (RTM), the edge was leakage, and the residual was not statistically retrievable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred play-type labels used as a clean measurement basis
failed_approaches.why: The audit failed on the OTHER share, low confidence and foul leakage (label error).
Cells were small (n_after 32-95) and no multiplicity correction was applied.

evidence_establishes: Own-sequence lags are not supported as a within-team effect. The global lifts were artifacts of team-quality confounding (FAM:SF-APPS-073, FAM:SF-CHT-029). The only residual noted was SPOT_UP lag-1.
Opponent next-possession suppression after a play type, where measured, is about 0.01-0.02 PPP and was real for 4 of 8 play types. DRIVE was not real by the record's test (FAM:SF-APPS-075).
The record describes these downstream effects as small relative to direct PPP gaps (FAM:SF-APPS-075).
The play-type labels failed an audit, so label error is a live threat to any play-type-level claim (FAM:SF-APPM-014).
Suppression labels selected on outcomes behave largely as RTM artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-086).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a 0.01-0.02 PPP downstream shift changes the ranking or assignment of any AVOID label, because the retrieved records do not state an AVOID threshold or run that test.
Whether the opponent-next-PPP effects survive a full within-team baseline plus game-state and ending-type controls. FAM:SF-APPS-075 does not record its baseline in the retrieved text.
Whether the lag results hold on 2025-26 data, or after label repair.
How the roughly 0.12-0.13 aftershock in FAM:SF07 relates to this question, since it is a different direction and estimand.
Whether FAM:SF-APPS-049's net-swing signs for DRIVE and POST_UP reflect downstream effects or the direct-PPP component, since net swing combines the two.
own_inferences: The 'large enough to drive AVOID labels' claim is probably false as stated. A 0.01-0.02 PPP shift is small next to direct PPP gaps, so it would rarely reorder labels unless labels sit near a threshold.

Part of the opponent-next-possession effect is probably mechanical. How play X ends (make versus miss versus turnover, and the resulting transition or inbound start) shapes the next possession's start type and PPP. Controls for ending type and next-possession start type are needed.
The near-uniform 0.12-0.13 aftershock across play types in FAM:SF07 suggests a shared offset, not play-type-specific causation. This is my inference.
With n>150k, p-values will be trivially small, so the test must be framed on effect size against a pre-specified practical threshold.
The 2025-26 playoffs are incomplete on the question date, so they cannot be used as a clean holdout until complete.
uncertainties: The AVOID label definition and its threshold are not given in the task or the retrieved records.
The baseline and controls used in FAM:SF-APPS-075 were not visible, because part of the record was cut. I did not call read_family.
The status of own-sequence lags after label repair is unknown.
Data completeness for 2025-26 on the posing date: the playoffs are partial until 2026-06-21.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, the question could have been run as a pooled lift test on the large n. The records show that global lifts were team-quality artifacts, that downstream effects are small, and that the labels are flawed. This moves the decision from proceed to proceed_with_changes: a within-team, effect-size test against a practical threshold, with label-quality and mechanical-ending controls, and own-sequence lag treated as a falsification target.

blocking_constraints.text: The label audit failed (OTHER 20.2%, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7%). Play-type attribution of downstream effects is unreliable unless restricted to high-confidence labels or label error is bounded.
Team quality, lineup, score margin and opponent defense drive the pooled lifts; only within-team estimates are interpretable.

prior_work.summary: Own-sequence lags were tested and recorded as artifacts, with no callable horizons. Opponent next-PPP suppression was estimated at about 0.01-0.02 PPP, real for 4 of 8 play types. Whether that is large enough to drive AVOID labels has not been tested directly. Label quality has failed an audit.

risks.text: Team-season quality, lineup, score margin, pace and opponent defense inflate pooled lifts, as shown in FAM:SF-APPS-073 and FAM:SF-CHT-029.
How play X ends (make, miss, turnover) determines the next possession's start type, and an AVOID label built from PPP is partly defined by the outcome.
After a made basket the opponent starts from an inbound, which constrains the next PPP, so downstream 'suppression' can arise from the ending type alone.
The audit found OTHER at 20.2%, 40.8% low confidence and foul possessions leaking into OTHER (FAM:SF-APPM-014).
Flagging play types or players as AVOID by extreme outcomes regresses toward the mean (FAM:SF-CHT-086).
Pooled n is huge, so p-values are uninformative, while team-by-play-type cells are small and noisy. Effect sizes of about 0.01-0.02 PPP need precision estimates.
8 play types, 5 lags, two directions and regular season versus playoffs create many comparisons (see the lack of correction in FAM:SF-APPA-050).
If AVOID labels and the downstream effect are computed on the same possessions, the label is validated on its own data. Estimate on one season block and evaluate on later ones.
Play-type mix and league efficiency shift across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so season-specific baselines are needed.
Possession-level PPP is a noisy outcome, and next-possession PPP is noisier still.

design.estimand: For each play type X, the within-team-season difference in opponent next-possession PPP (T+1) after the team ran X versus after the team's other possessions, adjusted for ending type, score margin, period, clock bucket and lineup tier. Secondarily, the effect on the same team's own next 1-5 possessions (lags 1-5) after the same demeaning. Then, the share of play types whose AVOID label (a pre-registered rule, to be fixed before analysis) changes when the downstream term is added to direct PPP. Practical threshold: 0.03 PPP. This is my proposal and is not taken from any record.
design.unit: Possession pairs (team possession T, next possession T+1) within game, with standard errors clustered by game and team-season.
design.sample: 2022-23 to 2024-25, regular season and playoffs, as development. 2025-26 regular season (complete) as the holdout. The 2025-26 playoffs are excluded until complete on 2026-06-21, then used as a sealed second holdout. Exclude possessions crossing period boundaries, garbage time (margin above a pre-set cutoff), and labels flagged OTHER or low confidence. Run a sensitivity analysis including them to bound label error.
design.power: Pooled n is above 150k per play type, so a 0.01 PPP SE is easy to reach. Pre-specify the minimum detectable effect from the clustered SE per play type and require the 95% CI half-width to be at most 0.015 PPP to call a null adequately powered. Team-level cells are not interpreted individually, only as a random-effects variance. Use shrinkage (empirical Bayes) for any per-team or per-player AVOID flag.
design.controls: Team-season fixed effects (demeaning), opponent-season defense rating, ending type of X (make, miss with defensive rebound, turnover, foul), start type of T+1 (inbound after make, rebound, steal), score margin, period, lineup tier, season. Compare with the global estimates to show the confound size, as in FAM:SF-APPS-073.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo: shuffle play-type labels within team-season-game-state strata and require the real effect to fall outside the placebo 95% range. (2) Lag-decay check: own-sequence effects must decay from lag 1 to lag 5, since flat lifts count as artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-029). (3) Pre-period check: the 'effect' of X on possession T-1 should be zero. (4) Replicate on the 2025-26 holdout with the same sign and an effect of at least half the development estimate.
design.multiplicity: 8 play types x 2 directions x 5 lags: Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05 within each family. Only the lag-1 contrast and the AVOID reclassification count are confirmatory. Everything else is exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if, for a play type, the within-team adjusted opponent T+1 shift is at least 0.03 PPP in the same direction, the BH-adjusted CI excludes 0.03 in development and holdout, and the AVOID label changes under the pre-registered rule. Rejected if the CI upper bound for the absolute shift is below 0.03 PPP in both periods (adequately powered null). Artifact if the pooled effect vanishes under demeaning or the placebo, or depends on ending type. Own-sequence lags are called callable only if they decay and survive demeaning. Otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the derived play-type possession records, 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season (complete 2026-04-13). The 2025-26 playoffs are partial on 2026-06-19 and complete from 2026-06-21. Freeze the file hash and label-pipeline version before analysis, and record the OTHER/low-confidence shares.

research_concepts: data quality of derived play-type records
methodological_questions: Is opponent next-possession PPP after a play type large enough to drive AVOID labels?
Do own-team previous-possession lags materially affect play-type outcomes?
How should sequential dependence be separated from confounding by game state, lineup, and opponent quality?
What sample size and shrinkage are needed for reliable play-type AVOID labels?
Is the derived play-type label outcome-dependent or subject to mechanical floor effects?
args.query: Effect of play type X on opponent next-possession PPP and own-sequence lags on AVOID labels in play-type labeling; prior findings, failed approaches, sample size, confounding, and label reliability

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
